title: PhD position in computational biocatalysis and enzyme design — applications close 15 September 2026
text:
CompBioCat is seeking a highly motivated PhD candidate to join BioReInt — Controlling Reactive Intermediates in Biocatalysis through Computational Design Tools — the group’s ERC Consolidator Grant, funded by the European Research Council.
BioReInt aims to develop next-generation computational enzyme engineering approaches that exploit highly reactive intermediates in enzymatic catalysis. Combining quantum chemistry, molecular dynamics simulations, machine learning, and protein and enzyme engineering, the project seeks to establish new design principles for biocatalysts capable of challenging and non-natural chemical transformations.
The successful candidate will work in an international, interdisciplinary environment at the IQCC, alongside experimental and computational collaborators worldwide, and will be trained in state-of-the-art computational tools for biocatalysis and enzyme design.

A background in computational chemistry
A basic understanding of organic chemistry and reaction mechanisms
Good written and spoken English
Interest and previous experience in scientific programming, preferably Python

Considered positively

Experience with quantum mechanical calculations, for example DFT
Experience with molecular dynamics simulations
Familiarity with Linux and Unix environments and high-performance computing
Biocatalysis, enzyme engineering or computational enzyme design

title: Hande Abeş and Aqza Elsa John at the NextGenBioCat meeting in Munich
text:
Hande Abeş and Aqza Elsa John, both PhD students in the group, attended the NextGenBioCat meeting in Munich.
Hande works on bridging scales in the computational modeling of biochemical and biocatalytic processes; Aqza works on the computational modeling of electrostatic confinement in biocatalysis.

title: Research
text:
Reactive intermediates in biocatalytic processes
Characterising short-lived, highly reactive intermediates in enzyme active sites, and using that control to unlock transformations enzymes do not perform in nature. Carbene and nitrene transfer, radical relay chemistry in nonheme iron enzymes, and selective oxidations.

Multiscale protocols in biocatalysis
Integrating QM, QM/MM, molecular dynamics, enhanced sampling and electrostatic analysis into workflows that connect conformational dynamics with chemical reactivity. Method development as much as application: understanding where current protocols break down when applied to biochemical systems.
